intro.title: Build a sortable and filterable table
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a dynamic table that displays data which can be sorted by column and filtered by a search term. You will learn how to manage and transform data arrays using JavaScript's built-in array methods like `sort()` and `filter()`. The core concepts involve handling state for the data and user inputs, and writing event handler functions to update the table. You'll create this interactive feature using plain JavaScript, HTML for structure, and CSS for basic styling, all within a single JavaScript file context.
intro.usecase: Sortable and filterable tables are essential UI components in data-intensive applications like e-commerce dashboards, admin panels, and analytics tools. For example, product managers use them to sort customer data by date or filter support tickets by status in platforms like Shopify or Zendesk. Developers implement these features to help users efficiently navigate large datasets, such as filtering inventory by category or sorting financial records by amount. Mastering this pattern enables you to build professional-grade interfaces that handle real-world data exploration needs.
